text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.
The hosts went trophyless last term, but their start to this one has Reds fans dreaming again of a silverware-laden season having tasted defeat just once in their first 13 games of the campaign.
They head into this one in fourth, but a win would move them three points behind leaders Tottenham.
After a solid start to the Premier League campaign, Forest have dropped off lately, winless in five games and just five points above the bottom three in 15th.
Their form on the road has been a huge issue with just one league win away from the City Ground since early January, coming against Chelsea earlier this season.

Jurgen Klopp makes seven changes from his team's 5-1 thumping of Toulouse in the Europa League in midweek as Alisson is reinstated between the sticks while Konate, Van Dijk and Tsimikas come into the back four.
Gravenberch impressed against Toulouse and keeps his place in midfield, where he will be joined by the returning Szoboszlai and Mac Allister, while Salah starts ahead of Elliott.
Luis Diaz is absent from the squad amid concerns over his family's welfare after his parents were kidnapped in his home country of Colombia.
His mother has been found, but his father remains missing.
Steve Cooper goes with a change of formation, playing with five defenders instead of the four he employed in the 2-2 home draw with Luton Town last weekend.
To accommodate the alteration in shape, Niakhate is preferred to Toffolo while Aina replaces Chris Wood.
The New Zealand international is absent altogether with a hamstring injury having netted both of Forest's goals against the Hatters.
The two sets of players enter the Anfield pitch and we are now moments away from this huge game in the Premier League.
The hosts kick us off and we are underway!
As you would perhaps expect, the hosts have done most of the running in these opening couple of minutes.
The visitors may have to soak up a lot of pressure if they are to come away with a surprise result.
Salah's delicate lofted pass finds Nunez in the box, but the Uruguay international does not get the power he wants on his volley and the ball trickles through to Turner.
Liverpool are unbeaten in their last 24 home league games against Forest (19 wins, five draws), since a 2-0 loss in February 1969.
The last four between the sides at Anfield has seen a total of 23 goals scored (5.8 per game – 16 for Liverpool, seven for Forest).
A first real foray forward for the visitors ends with Elanga flashing a shot wide of the left post.
Forest have gotten through the opening 10 minutes at Anfield, where so many teams have crumbled previously.
Cooper will be encouraged by his team's start.
The away side has never won in 12 Premier League meetings between Liverpool and Forest – only Aston Villa vs Queens Park Rangers has been played more often without an away victory (14).
Mac Allister drags a long-range effort well wide of the left post as Forest continue to defend resiliently.
The sole away win this season for Cooper's men came at Stamford Bridge against Chelsea, where they had to do a lot of defending before Elanga scored the winner on the counter.
Can they replicate that display here?
Alexander-Arnold receives the first booking of the contest for a late challenge on Aina as the visiting defender tried to clear upfield.
The home fans want a penalty as Nunez is sent tumbling by Boly, though they are half-hearted shouts at best and the referee instead points for a corner.
Alexander-Arnold's fierce drive from distance is bravely blocked by Sangare's head.
The midfielder feels the full effect of the shot and will require some treatment.
Sangare looks a little worse for wear, but he eventually returns to his feet and play resumes.
Liverpool are on top at the moment, but Forest are so far restricting them to long-range efforts and half-chances.
Elanga is looking increasingly isolated up top as his team is forced back by wave after wave of Liverpool attack.
Turner makes a comfortable save to deny Nunez's shot from a tight angle, before the Liverpool forward heads well over the crossbar from the resulting corner.
GOAL!!! JOTA FIRES LIVERPOOL IN FRONT!!! A swift move from the hosts sees Salah slide a neat throughball into the path of Nunez, who fires goalwards.
The forward's effort is saved by Turner, but the Forest goalkeeper can only parry back into the danger area, where Jota is on hand to tap home the rebound and put the hosts 1-0 up!
Mangala goes in the book for a foul on Jota in midfield.
GOAL!!! NUNEZ MAKES IT 2-0!!! Jota picks out Szoboszlai in midfield before the Hungary international plays a lovely one-two with Salah.
Szoboszlai manages to dig out a cross, and Nunez is waiting in the middle to turn home and put Liverpool firmly in the driver's seat!
Szoboszlai played an integral part in the goal, linking up with Salah before putting it on a plate for Nunez.
Nunez has now contributed to goals in his last four games in the Premier League (two goals, two assists).
He can certainly still frustrate, but there is no doubt things are starting to come together for the former Benfica man.
Liverpool are pressing hard for a third to potentially put this game to bed.
Turner is required twice in a matter of seconds to deny Gravenberch and then Szoboszlai.
The latter of those saves was a superb stop to deny Szoboszlai's powerful goalbound effort.
Nunez goes for the spectacular as he tries a bicycle kick from near the edge of the box.
It is a decent effort, too, though it does clear the crossbar by a good couple of yards.
Forest try and grab a goal back before half-time as Boly nods a free-kick delivery back for Murillo to hit, but the 21-year-old gets his first-time shot badly wrong as he slices well wide.
We are into four minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Liverpool have lost just one of their last 46 Premier League games at Anfield (W35 D10), a 2-1 defeat to Leeds United on October 29 last year.
They are unbeaten in 16 home games since then (W13 D3), a record that looks set to be extended here.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 2-0 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
The teams head back to the changing rooms at Anfield with Liverpool in control, 2-0 up thanks to goals from Jota and Nunez.
Klopp's men were dominating possession and territory but struggled to break through a resilient Forest defence.
However, with 31 minutes on the clock, a clever move ended with Nunez's drive parried by Turner, straight into the path of Jota who gleefully finished the rebound.
It would be 2-0 just four minutes later thanks to excellent work by Szoboszlai, playing a lovely one-two with Salah before crossing for Nunez to tap home to put the Reds in command at the interval.
Forest had just 25.7 per cent of possession in that opening 45 minutes and are yet to have a shot on target.
Cooper would have expected a tough outing at Anfield, but he will surely be frustrated by just how little his team have shown going forward.
The visitors get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Salah cuts onto his dangerous left foot and tries to pick out the far corner, but he does not get it quite right and the ball loops over the target.
After not drawing consecutive games across any of their first 44 games back in the Premier League between August 2022 and September 2023, Forest have drawn all three games in October.
Forest have not drawn four consecutive league games since January 2016, a run that looks likely to continue here.
Dominguez cynically drags back Alexander-Arnold and receives a yellow card.
Salah has been directly involved in 17 goals in his last 13 Premier League appearances at Anfield for Liverpool (14 goals, three assists), either scoring or assisting in every appearance.
He is yet to register a goal involvement in this outing, though.
The visitors have accumulated just 0.13 xG (expected goals) so far.
They will have to create more in attack if they are to pull off an unlikely comeback.
Mac Allister is booked for wiping out Gibbs-White in midfield.
Jota opened the scoring but now makes way for Gakpo.
Gravenberch is replaced by Elliott.
Just under half an hour to play at Anfield and Liverpool are in almost complete control.
Their lead is only the two goals, though, and Klopp will be wanting a third soon to avoid any late nerves.
Salah picks himself up off the turf after being felled by Murillo to let fly from the resulting free-kick, though he can only curl high and wide of the target.
Forest are showing little signs of life in attack, yet to have an attempt in this second half.
Liverpool have not lost a home Premier League game against a team whose name begins with 'N' since losing 1-0 to Norwich City in April 1994, going 40 unbeaten at Anfield since (33 wins, seven draws).
Alexander-Arnold lets fly with an ambitious effort from all of 30 yards out, but it proves to be a poor decision as he fires off target.
Cooper makes his first changes, bringing on Yates for Dominguez.
Aina makes way for Toffolo.
Cooper brings on Awoniyi for Boly in an attacking substitution.
The hosts have had 18 shots, compared to just two for their opponents.
It has been a dominant performance from Liverpool.
Liverpool are continuing to press for a third that would surely put this game beyond the visitors' reach, if it was not already.
15 minutes to play at Anfield and Klopp's side still lead by just the two goals.
If Forest pull one back, it could be a nervy remainder of the game for the hosts.
GOAL!!! SALAH PUTS IT TO BED!!! It is an absolute howler from Turner, who races out of his goal to try and cut out Szoboszlai's punted ball upfield.
The Forest goalkeeper completely misjudges the bounce of the ball and Salah latches onto it, coolly finishing to make it 3-0 and surely wrap up the three points for Liverpool!
Szoboszlai's lofted throughball was in hope more than expectation, though Salah was on hand to take full advantage of Turner's mistake.
Nunez had a big hand in the first two goals and now makes way for Endo.
Gakpo cuts onto his right foot before unleashing a drive towards the bottom corner, though it goes the wrong side of the post for Liverpool and instead crashes into the side-netting.
Gibbs-White trudges off for Williams.
Santos enters the fray for Mangala.
An almighty scramble in the Liverpool has Forest players claiming for a penalty, though the protests are to no avail as the referee waves play on.
OFF THE BAR! Yates' deep cross picks out Elanga at the back post.
The former Manchester United man catches his left-footed volley sweetly, but the ball crashes off the woodwork and away from danger.
Another chance for Forest goes begging as another delivery finds Elanga at the back post, but this time, his volley never troubles Alisson's goal as he smashes over and into the stands.
Alexander-Arnold is replaced by Gomez.
As Liverpool come forward on the counter, Sangare takes out Gakpo and picks up a yellow card.
We are into four minutes of additional time.
Forest are finally showing some attacking intent, though it has come far too late for it to have any impact.
GOAL!!! GAKPO MAKES IT 4-0!!! With seconds remaining, another intricate move ends with Elliott firing across the face of goal.
Gakpo is there in the middle, and he prods home to cap the victory for Liverpool! There will be a VAR check, though...
NO GOAL!!! The replays show that Gakpo was a good couple of yards offside and the goal is ruled out.
The score remains 3-0 to Liverpool!
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 3-0 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
The full-time whistle blows as Liverpool run out comfortable 3-0 victors at Anfield against a below-par Forest.

Jota set them on their way to three points as he prodded home the rebound from Nunez's parried shot, before the Uruguay international netted himself just four minutes later, turning Szoboszlai's cross into the back of the net to put the hosts in control at the interval.

Any hopes of a Forest comeback were ended after the break, Turner making a huge error in misjudging the bounce of Szoboszlai's punt upfield, a mistake that Salah took full advantage of as he coolly finished to seal the win, one that moves Liverpool onto 23 points, just three behind leaders Tottenham.
For Forest, their winless run extends to six games, a streak that Cooper will be keen to halt with his team just five points above the drop zone.
That is all we have for you from Anfield, so thanks for your company and goodbye!
